seoTitle: How to Paste Code in TradingView (Pine Script)
metaDescription: Learn how to open the Pine Editor, paste Pine Script code correctly, save it, and apply it to your TradingView chart without compile errors.
intro: Adding a custom indicator or strategy to TradingView means working with Pine Script inside the Pine Editor, and pasting code incorrectly is one of the most common reasons scripts fail to compile. This guide shows the right way to open the editor, paste your code, save it, and apply it to a chart.

steps.heading: Open the Pine Editor
steps.body: From the bottom panel of any TradingView chart, open the Pine Editor tab where you can write or paste script code.

steps.heading: Paste the code correctly
steps.body: Clear any placeholder script first, then paste your indicator or strategy code into the editor without leaving stray characters from the copy source.

steps.heading: Save the script
steps.body: Save the script with a clear name so you can find and reuse it later from your list of personal scripts.

steps.heading: Add it to your chart
steps.body: Use the 'Add to chart' button in the Pine Editor to apply the compiled script directly onto your active chart.

steps.heading: Fix common compile errors
steps.body: If the script doesn't compile, check for mismatched Pine Script version declarations, missing indicator() or strategy() calls, or formatting issues introduced during copy-paste.

faq.question: Why won't my pasted Pine Script compile?
faq.answer: This usually happens from a version mismatch, missing declaration line, or extra characters picked up when copying the code from another source.

faq.question: What's the difference between an indicator and a strategy in Pine Script?
faq.answer: Indicators display analysis on a chart, while strategies simulate trades with entries and exits so you can backtest performance.

faq.question: Do I need a paid plan to use the Pine Editor?
faq.answer: No, the Pine Editor is available on TradingView's free plan, though script limits can vary by plan.

faq.question: Can I edit a script after pasting it?
faq.answer: Yes, you can edit the code directly in the Pine Editor and re-save or re-apply it to update the version on your chart.
